method: AI-assisted editorial source-level review of a declared priority batch. The Bible is the authoritative foundation; supporting historical and archaeological sources are limited to the claims and access scope recorded here. No independent specialist signoff is claimed.
deferred: Nine assessed place dossiers still need external archaeological bibliography; regional placeholders were not upgraded.
The other 107 explained pairs retain their existing review labels and have no new source-level assessment in this batch.
Other person-trail access gaps, full excavation reports, manuscript apparatuses, wider source coverage and independent specialist review remain open.
The full OpenBible corpus remains unclassified.

records.title: Birth, Egypt and Nazareth
records.note: Matthew includes flight to Egypt and return after Herod; Luke moves from the temple presentation to Nazareth. Their combined map sequence is an editorial arrangement.
records.limitation: No extra trip, elapsed interval or harmonised calendar is established by this check.

records.title: Temple scenes
records.note: John places its temple scene near the beginning of the ministry; Mark places its scene after the Jerusalem entry. Both passages remain available for comparison.
records.limitation: These literary positions do not decide whether the accounts describe one action or more. Existing specialist literature was not fully reviewed.

records.title: Hometown synagogue order
records.note: Luke presents the synagogue rejection before its Capernaum sequence; Mark presents a hometown rejection after earlier Galilean episodes.
records.limitation: The check supports retaining the ordering question; it does not settle whether these are the same encounter.

records.title: Fishermen and Capernaum
records.note: Mark narrates the call before the Capernaum synagogue; Luke narrates the fishing and call after earlier Capernaum ministry.
records.limitation: No precise common date or additional encounter is inferred.

citations.supports: Capernaum and call sequence in Luke

records.title: Jairus at the shore
records.note: Mark places the gathering beside the sea after a crossing and names Jairus, without naming Capernaum at this point. The existing regional location is retained.
records.limitation: A later house scene does not identify an excavated house or an exact meeting point.

citations.supports: Lakeshore wording and absence of a named town

records.title: Feeding near Bethsaida
records.note: Luke names Bethsaida in the withdrawal and then describes a deserted setting for the crowd. A town name does not yield a surveyed feeding point.
records.limitation: Only Luke's selected context was rechecked here; parallel accounts and landscape reconstruction require further comparison.

records.title: Caesarea Philippi district
records.note: Matthew locates the confession in the district of Caesarea Philippi. The Banias report supplies archaeological context for the ancient site.
records.limitation: The report does not locate the conversation at the cave, temple or any particular building.

records.title: Samaria and Galilee corridor
records.note: Luke describes travel between Samaria and Galilee and entry into a village without naming the village.
records.limitation: No modern boundary, road or precise crossing point is inferred.

records.title: John 7:53-8:11 textual note
records.note: The ESV publisher marks the passage with a note about its absence from the earliest manuscripts. The existing feast entry continues from John 8:12.
records.limitation: This records a publisher textual note, not an independent manuscript collation or a verdict on the passage's theological use.

records.title: Bethany anointing accounts
records.note: John introduces the Bethany dinner six days before Passover; Mark narrates an anointing after its two-days-before-Passover introduction.
records.limitation: Narrative framing alone does not establish two separate dinners, resolve chronology or prove additional journeys.

records.title: Village ahead of the disciples
records.note: Mark names the approach to Bethphage and Bethany, then describes a village opposite the disciples. The retrieval village is not explicitly equated with Bethphage.
records.limitation: No exact village footprint or retrieval street is assigned.

citations.supports: Named approach and subsequent village instruction

records.title: Jericho approach and departure
records.note: Luke describes approach to Jericho; Mark describes departure. The existing qualification remains beside the combined entry.
records.limitation: A proposed old-town/new-town solution needs separate historical evidence; no such solution is asserted here.

records.title: Supper and Passover
records.note: John opens the supper before Passover and later describes the authorities preparing to eat Passover. Mark explicitly frames preparation for the meal as Passover.
records.limitation: Retain the calendar warning. These selected passages do not establish one undisputed harmonised date; the previously linked research article was not reviewed in full.

records.title: Golgotha and later commemorations
records.note: John names Golgotha near the city and describes a garden and tomb nearby. The map continues to distinguish those biblical settings from modern commemorative coordinates.
records.limitation: No excavation report was assessed for a particular trial room or tomb in this batch. Existing heritage links do not supply event-level identification.

records.title: Appearance sequence
records.note: Luke 24 groups Emmaus and Jerusalem appearances; John 20 explicitly distinguishes a later gathering involving Thomas.
records.limitation: Selected context checks do not establish a continuously dated route across all appearance accounts.

records.title: Eastern lake names
records.note: Mark's publisher note records an alternative Gadarenes reading alongside Gerasenes. The regional marker and textual warning are retained.
records.limitation: No manuscript apparatus or complete Gospel-variant comparison was undertaken; Gergesenes and exact landing proposals need fuller source review.

records.title: Bethsaida candidate review
records.note: The el-Araj 2024 report describes Byzantine remains and earlier walls, with several identifications explicitly provisional. It does not settle the el-Araj versus et-Tell comparison.
records.limitation: The project report was readable in this review, closing the landing-page access gap. Comparative excavation publications from et-Tell and independent assessment remain outstanding; no candidate receives a confidence upgrade.

citations.locator: 2024 season report, Areas E, A and D
citations.supports: Reported excavation context and the project's provisional identifications only
